original_question: We say that a product XY = {xy | x ∈ X, y ∈ Y } of two subsets X, Y of a group G is direct if for every z ∈ XY there are unique x ∈ X, y ∈ Y such that z = xy. Is there an infinite group G such that every subset A ⊆ G satisfies the following property: all the maximal subsets B for which the product AB is direct have the same cardinality? Note that for checking the property for a given infinite group G, it suffices to consider only those subsets A ⊆ G for which |A| = |G \ A|. Indeed, the property is equivalent to A−1 A ∩ BB −1 = {1} and A−1 AB = G, and these imply |G| = |A||B|, since G is infinite. Now, if |A| < |G \ A|, then |A| < |G|, and so |B| = |G|; and if |A| > |G \ A|, then A−1 A = G, and so |B| = 1, for all B satisfying the property.
target_in_paper: Problem 21.58 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)" of the current arXiv version of Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper extremely closely: it gives the paper's definition of a direct product AB of subsets of a group, asks exactly for an infinite group G with the stated uniform-cardinality property for maximal B, and includes the author's note that, for checking the property in an infinite group, it is enough to look at subsets A with |A| = |G \ A|, together with the equivalent conditions involving A^{-1}A, BB^{-1}, and A^{-1}AB. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
missing_details: Make explicit that "maximal subsets B" means maximal by inclusion among subsets B ⊆ G for which AB is direct; that is implicit in the paper's wording. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))

If the reduction note is retained, define the notation A^{-1} = {a^{-1} : a ∈ A}, A^{-1}A = {a^{-1}a' : a, a' ∈ A}, and BB^{-1} = {bb'^{-1} : b, b' ∈ B}, since the paper uses this notation without re-expanding it there. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
If the reduction note is retained, spell out that G \ A denotes the set-theoretic complement of A in G. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))

For full stand-alone clarity, one may restate "AB is direct" as injectivity of the multiplication map A × B → G, (a, b) ↦ ab; the paper states this as uniqueness of representation. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
refined_question: Does there exist an infinite group G such that, for every subset A ⊆ G, all subsets B ⊆ G that are maximal by inclusion subject to the condition that the product AB = {ab : a ∈ A, b ∈ B} is direct—that is, every element of AB has a unique representation ab with a ∈ A and b ∈ B—have the same cardinality? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, does there exist an infinite group G such that, for every subset A ⊆ G, all subsets B ⊆ G satisfying A^{-1}A ∩ BB^{-1} = {1} and A^{-1}AB = G have the same cardinality? Here A^{-1} = {a^{-1} : a ∈ A}, A^{-1}A = {a^{-1}a' : a, a' ∈ A}, and BB^{-1} = {bb'^{-1} : b, b' ∈ B}; the paper states that these two conditions are equivalent to B being maximal among the subsets for which AB is direct. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
justification: The draft is essentially the official formulation of Problem 21.58 itself, with the author's explanatory note attached. The only sharpening needed to make it fully stand-alone and paper-faithful is to state maximality as maximality by inclusion and, if the note is kept, to unpack the inverse-product notation used there. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
